content: Formoterol is a medication that has been associated with an increased risk of serious or fatal asthma-related complications in certain patients. In a large clinical study, individuals using asthma medications similar to formoterol experienced a higher rate of asthma-related deaths compared to those who did not use such medications. If you have asthma, using formoterol may elevate the risk of severe or life-threatening asthma problems. Your doctor will only prescribe formoterol if other treatments have failed to adequately control your asthma or if your asthma is so severe that it requires the use of two medications for proper management. Formoterol should never be the first or sole medication used to treat asthma. Do not use formoterol if your asthma is rapidly worsening. Inform your doctor if you have experienced frequent severe asthma attacks or if you have ever been hospitalized due to asthma symptoms. If you notice any of the following signs of worsening asthma, contact your doctor immediately: Your short-acting inhaler is less effective than before. You need to use more puffs or use your short-acting inhaler more frequently than usual. You require four or more puffs of your short-acting inhaler daily for two or more consecutive days. You use more than one canister (200 inhalations) of your short-acting inhaler within an eight-week period. Your peak-flow meter readings indicate worsening breathing. You require emergency room treatment for asthma. Your symptoms fail to improve after one week of regular formoterol use or worsen at any point during treatment. Discuss the risks of using formoterol with your doctor. You will receive a Medication Guide from your doctor or pharmacist when you begin treatment and each time you refill your prescription. Read this guide carefully and ask any questions you may have. Additional information can be found on the FDA website or the manufacturer’s website. Formoterol is prescribed to alleviate wheezing, shortness of breath, and breathing difficulties caused by asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), which includes chronic bronchitis and emphysema. It is also used to prevent exercise-induced bronchospasm. Formoterol belongs to a class of medications known as long-acting beta agonists (LABAs), which work by relaxing and opening the airways in the lungs, facilitating easier breathing. Formoterol is available as a powder-filled capsule for oral inhalation using a specific inhaler. If prescribed for asthma or COPD, it is typically inhaled twice daily, once in the morning and once in the evening, with doses spaced 12 hours apart. If used to prevent exercise-induced breathing difficulties, it should be inhaled at least 15 minutes before exercise, but not more than once every 12 hours. If you are already using formoterol twice daily, do not take an additional dose before exercising. Follow your prescription instructions precisely and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not alter your dosage or frequency without medical advice. If you are taking other asthma medications, your doctor will provide guidance on how to use them alongside formoterol. For example, if you are on a corticosteroid to prevent airway inflammation, you will likely continue using it as before. If you were regularly using a short-acting beta agonist inhaler like albuterol, your doctor may advise discontinuing regular use but continuing to use it for sudden asthma symptoms. Formoterol is not intended to stop an ongoing asthma or COPD attack; a short-acting inhaler will be prescribed for such emergencies. Do not stop using formoterol without consulting your doctor, as abrupt discontinuation may worsen your symptoms. Before using the formoterol inhaler for the first time, ask your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist to demonstrate its proper use. Practice under their supervision. Follow these steps to use the inhaler: 1. Check the expiration date on the box and attach the provided sticker to the inhaler cover as a reminder of when to stop using it. 2. Open the foil pouch containing the blister card of capsules. Do not remove a capsule until you are ready to use it. 3. Remove the inhaler cover and twist the mouthpiece open. 4. Separate one blister from the card, peel back the foil, and push the capsule through. 5. Place the capsule in the chamber (not the mouthpiece) and close the inhaler. 6. Hold the inhaler upright and press both side buttons simultaneously to puncture the capsule. Release the buttons. 7. Exhale fully, but not into the inhaler. 8. Hold the inhaler level, place the mouthpiece in your mouth, and inhale quickly and deeply. You should taste the medication and hear a whirring noise. If not, the capsule may be stuck; tap the inhaler gently and repeat the steps without pressing the buttons again. 9. Remove the inhaler and hold your breath for as long as comfortable before exhaling. 10. Check the capsule for remaining powder. If any remains, repeat the inhalation process. 11. Once the capsule is empty, discard it and close the inhaler. The inhaler is designed to pierce the capsule and release the powder. Occasionally, the capsule may break into small pieces, but the inhaler’s screen prevents these from reaching your mouth. Proper storage and handling of the capsules can minimize this risk. Capsules should remain in their foil packaging until use and should only be handled with dry hands. Do not use the inhaler with a spacer or exhale into the device. Keep the inhaler dry and replace it with a new one when refilling your prescription. Before using formoterol, inform your doctor if you are allergic to formoterol, other medications, or milk proteins. Do not use formoterol with other LABAs, such as fluticasone-salmeterol (Advair) or salmeterol (Serevent). Provide your doctor with a complete list of all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, as certain drugs may interact with formoterol. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor immediately. Formoterol may cause side effects. Minor side effects include nervousness, headache, tremors, dry mouth, muscle cramps, back pain, nausea, heartburn, stomach pain, fatigue, dizziness, insomnia, nasal congestion, and sore throat. Severe side effects, such as swelling, hoarseness, difficulty breathing or swallowing, hives, rash, chest pain, or irregular heartbeat, require immediate medical attention. Store formoterol capsules in their original packaging at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Keep them out of reach of children. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and replace your inhaler with each prescription refill. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center or emergency services immediately. Symptoms of overdose may include chest pain, fainting, rapid or irregular heartbeat, nervousness, headache, tremors, seizures, muscle cramps, dry mouth, nausea, dizziness, fatigue, insomnia, excessive thirst, or difficulty breathing. Keep all medical appointments and do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refills. Formoterol is marketed under brand names such as Foradil® and Aerolizer®.
